title: Getting Your Share Sale Money Instantly: What T+0 Settlement Means
description: T+0 settlement means you get your money on the very same day you sell shares in the stock market. India's market regulator, SEBI, has made T+0 settlement opti.

faq.a: T+1 settlement means that the transfer of shares to the buyer and money to the seller happens one business day after the trade is executed. This is currently the standard settlement cycle for most stocks in India.

faq.q: Which stocks are currently under T+0 settlement?
faq.a: As of 2026, T+0 settlement is optionally available for the top 500 stocks by market capitalisation on NSE and BSE. SEBI began this rollout in phases from January 2025, adding 100 stocks each month. You can usually find the list of eligible stocks on the NSE and BSE websites or through your stockbroker.

faq.q: Do I need to do anything different for T+0 trades?
faq.a: For eligible stocks, your broker will likely offer the T+0 option. You might need to select this option when placing your trade, and ensure it's done within the specified trading window (typically before 1:30 PM).

faq.q: Will T+0 settlement become mandatory for all stocks?
faq.a: While SEBI has been progressively shortening settlement cycles, the current T+0 system is optional. The regulator is evaluating its impact and operational aspects, and future decisions on making it mandatory or expanding it further will depend on market readiness and experience.

faq.q: How does T+0 benefit the Indian stock market overall?
faq.a: T+0 settlement enhances market efficiency, reduces systemic risk, and improves liquidity by speeding up the movement of funds and securities. It also aligns India's capital markets with global best practices and positions the country as a leader in financial innovation.
